05 / Selectable CSS

Clipping changes paint, not the layout box

Percentages use a border-box with zero border and padding; the last vertex closes to the first. Simple concave rings and straight-through redundant points are allowed. This tool rejects duplicates, overlap, touch, crossings and zero area; these are not all CSS grammar restrictions. Apply Concave L, introduce a crossing, then repair it using the reported edge labels. Changing dimensions changes pixels and area, not percentage CSS.

The schematic labels P vertices and E edges; the native preview shows only clipped pattern paint. The outside outline retains the full layout size. Exact table fractions are authoritative: approx. 0.000 does not mean exact zero area. Output is one CSS declaration, without dimensions or pattern; check context when adopting other borders, padding or content.

Synthetic numbers stay in memory: no uploads, storage, URL state or Clipboard API. Single-line inputs may strip CR/LF; language switching retains raw text. Reload restores defaults; BFCache return clears old results.
